s1.syndrome_frame: Painless vulvar mass with gradual enlargement
salient_findings: Painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region
Mass enlargement over the past four months
12cm, non-tender mass of the right labia majora
Well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass on soft-tissue ultrasound
key_facts: 67-year-old woman
Painless right vulvar mass
Mass first noted two years earlier
Gradual enlargement over the past four months
No pain, changes in appetite or bowel habits, urinary symptoms, weight loss, infection, or bleeding
Hypertension managed with valsartan/amlodipine
Hysterectomy in 2016 for abnormal uterine bleeding
Post-menopausal
No history of hormone therapy
Does not smoke or drink alcohol
Afebrile with normal vital signs
Abdominal exam unremarkable
12cm, non-tender mass of the right labia majora
No erythema, lymphadenopathy, or signs of inflammation
Pelvic exam otherwise normal
Soft-tissue ultrasound showed a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass
Mild peripheral blood flow on Doppler imaging
Routine laboratory results within normal limits

shortlist.label: Canal of Nuck hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the leading preoperative impression and the patient's presentation of a painless vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of a painless vulvar mass, especially given the mass's gradual enlargement and the patient's post-menopausal status

shortlist.label: Vulvar lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a painless vulvar mass, although less likely given the mass's size and location

shortlist.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less common, it is a possible cause of a vulvar mass, especially in post-menopausal women

shortlist.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare cause of a vulvar mass, but still a possibility given the patient's presentation and the mass's characteristics

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a painless, gradually enlarging vulvar mass extending into the inguinal region, along with ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass tracking into the inguinal canal, is consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia, especially given the preoperative impression.

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a slow-growing, painless mass, but often has a more infiltrative appearance on imaging.

rejected.label: Vulvar lipoma
rejected.why: Would likely appear more echogenic on ultrasound and may not extend into the inguinal canal.

rejected.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a painful mass and may have associated lymphadenopathy or other signs of malignancy, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
rejected.why: May present as a solid mass, but the location and extension into the inguinal canal are not typical for this diagnosis.
